title: Latency Amplification Probe: Mixed-Profile Continuous Batching and Queueing Benchmark
creator: Priya Shah
description: Objective: Quantify and characterize latency amplification caused by continuous batching interacting with queueing under mixed arrival profiles and heterogeneous model variants. Background: Prior harnesses explore batching and tail effects in isolation; this probe aims to reproduce realistic app patterns (short chat turns, long generation jobs, periodic bursts) and measure how continuous batching heuristics + queueing amplify p95/p99 under varying concurrency, KV cache warmness, and model quantization. Scope: build a repeatable load harness that: 1) generates multi-class arrival traces, 2) models session affinity and prefix caching, 3) exercises kernel selection/quantization variants, 4) captures token/sec and tail latency surfaces, and 5) implements automated regression detection. Success criteria: 1) reproducible p95/p99 surfaces across runs (variance <5% for baseline), 2) detection rules that alert on p95 regression > 10% with <2 false positives per 24h synthetic run, 3) identify at least two configuration interactions causing >20% latency amplification (batching window, queueing watermark, read-from-cache ratio). Acceptance: benchmark artifacts (configs, arrival traces, dashboards, analysis notebook), a draft RFC for mitigation strategies (e.g., jittered batching windows, priority queueing, adaptive batch caps), and a follow-up ENG spike to pilot mitigations on dedicated cluster.
steps: Design mixed-profile trace generator: short-chat (30-100 tokens, high arrival rate), long-gen (500-2048 tokens, low rate), background-embeddings (embedding requests interleaved).
Implement session affinity + prefix KV cache simulation to vary cache hit ratio from 0% to 90%.
Create arrival schedules: steady-state, periodic microbursts, bimodal bursts, and adversarial probe (sustained high short-turn ratio).
Parameterize runtime knobs: batching window (1-50ms), max batch size, queue watermarks, backpressure thresholds, model variant mix (float32, int8-quant, Lv3-optimized).
Instrument metrics export: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, queued-ms per request, batch size distribution, cache hit rate, GPU utilization, and kernel selection counts.
Run controlled sweep matrix across knobs and arrival schedules; collect 10 repetitions per cell for statistical confidence.
Apply regression detectors (CUSUM on p95, EWMA drift, sliding-window percent change) and surface findings to dashboard with linked diffs to baseline.
Draft mitigation experiments and schedule canary runs on dedicated infra if probe shows production-significant regressions.

monitoring_queries: Grafana panel queries to compute batch size distribution: sum(rate(batch_size_count[5m])) by (batch_size)
p95 latency per model variant: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_variant))
results_summary: Preliminary runs show a consistent pattern: when short-chat traffic exceeds 60% of arrivals and cache hit ratio is below 40%, p95 amplifies 18-35% versus baseline due to batch composition skew (batches include a few long-gen requests that block batch completion). CUSUM detector currently flags the majority of these regressions within a 3-8 minute window. Next steps: add per-batch composition metrics, evaluate jittered batching window and priority queueing to reduce amplification, and run mitigation canaries on dedicated cluster.
